daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo has ordered a forensic audit of hajj financial management following concerns over cost allocation, with the president requesting that the cost burden not fall heavily on pilgrims and suggesting a 52:48 cost-sharing formula. The issue of Lapas Cibinong's luxury facilities continued to dominate parliamentary attention today. DPR members told the Director General of Corrections to resign if unable to handle the job, while the Director General defended his agency by stating there was no budget for CCTV installation in prisons and detention centres.

  • Komisi II DPR met with the Ombudsman today to discuss findings from the Lapas Cibinong inspection, which uncovered 13 luxury cluster houses not registered in the state asset system.
  • The Constitutional Court case challenging Vice President Gibran's educational qualifications has entered the evidentiary phase, marking a new stage in the legal dispute.
  • The 10th National Congress of AMPI (Association of Indonesian Muslim Intellectuals) is being held today, with Zigo Rolanda reportedly the sole candidate for leadership.
  • President Prabowo paid a condolence visit to Megawati's residence, with PDI-P official Said Abdullah describing the meeting as "very personal."
  • An advocate has challenged the minimum age requirement for ad hoc judge candidates at the Constitutional Court.
  • A researcher has filed a Constitutional Court challenge against the requirement that new political parties must have physical offices.
  • The Jakarta South District Court will read the pretrial ruling for Silmy Karim this afternoon.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Trade Minister departed for the United States to attend a G20 meeting, representing Indonesia in multilateral trade discussions. Separately, President Prabowo and Turkish President Erdogan held talks on trade, defence cooperation, and Turkey's COP31 invitation to Indonesia. The Indonesian Navy is set to receive 105 US amphibious combat vehicles by 2028, strengthening maritime defence capabilities.

  • The Indonesian Red Cross reaffirmed its support for Palestine in meetings with Palestinian representatives.
  • A DPD member from Papua endorsed the TNI's firm stance against the OPM armed group, while cautioning that civilian casualties must be avoided.
  • Indonesia is training African officials to expand trade and investment ties as part of South-South cooperation efforts.
  • Arab countries conveyed condolences to Indonesia over the sinking of the KMP Virgo ferry.

Other

Bank Indonesia kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at 5.75 percent, citing stable inflation conditions, while preparing monetary strategies to safeguard the rupiah against the US dollar amid expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in Q4 due to surging energy prices. On the health front, the Health Ministry emphasized that oseltamivir for Influenza A is safe but warned against indiscriminate consumption as concerns rise during flu season.

  • The government is allocating 5.67 million hectares of forest for food production, energy, and services, while separately fast-tracking five livestock zones to boost domestic food production.
  • Energy Minister Bahlil has prohibited subsidiaries from operating mines unless they have approval from parent companies, tightening mining sector governance.
  • The Transportation Minister explained that Indonesia has not yet approved plans to import used trains from Japan for commuter rail expansion.
  • Police headquarters has taken over the investigation into the KM Virgo ferry accident, with five more bodies recovered from the wreck.
  • The government launched a program to prepare Gen Z for life skills beyond formal employment opportunities.
